features.title: Python and Spark SQL, together
features.description: Use Python and Spark SQL together for Lakehouse Files and Delta Tables in the same dependency model.

features.title: Ordinary T-SQL
features.description: Keep ordinary SELECTs, without a proprietary modelling language or macros.

features.title: Native Power BI
features.description: Add enterprise power to your Power BI models and reports, while keeping to native PBIP, TMDL and native Report definitions.

features.title: Windows, macOS, Linux, or just Fabric Notebooks
features.description: Develop and operate Weaver projects on Windows, macOS or Linux, or work entirely inside Fabric Notebooks. Build and deploy native Power BI models and Reports without Power BI Desktop or a Windows computer.

features.title: Built for developers and AI agents
features.description: Readable terminal output for developers, and structured `--json` results, previews and no prompts for AI agents. A guide covers running an agent against a development workspace.

features.title: One dependency graph across Fabric
features.description: Order selected managed Lakehouse work, Warehouse T-SQL and dependent Semantic Model refreshes in one DAG.

features.title: Generated Warehouse pipelines
features.description: A SELECT becomes a Table with generated staging, declared-key matching, row-change reconciliation and recorded results.

features.title: Managed Lakehouse pipelines
features.description: Materialise Files, Python and Spark SQL into managed Delta Tables without hand-building another orchestration project.

features.title: Dependency discovery
features.description: Python imports and supported T-SQL references supply dependencies; Spark SQL uses explicit declarations.

features.title: Incremental inserts, updates and deletes
features.description: Apply insert/update candidates and explicit delete keys under the declared policy, without rebuilding every target.

features.title: Per-consumer bookmarks
features.description: Each loadable Table or Folder keeps its own clean processing boundary, even when consumers share a source.

features.title: Tests and Assumptions
features.description: Compare expected and actual results or catch rule-breaking rows through supported Python, SQL and DAX validations.

features.title: Data-quality safeguards
features.description: Record rejected input and refuse proposed update/delete changes that exceed active stability thresholds.

features.title: Organisation-wide modelling standards
features.description: Apply shared native TMDL policy across Semantic Models instead of repeating formats and conventions.

features.title: Built-in modelling annotations
features.description: Hide foreign keys, generate measure selectors and apply supported model rules through native TMDL annotations.

features.title: Custom Python annotations
features.description: Implement project-specific modelling conventions in trusted Python when native policy and built-ins are not enough.

features.title: Semantic Model composition
features.description: Reuse a native model foundation to produce audience variants without maintaining complete copies.

features.title: DAX validation and SQL reconciliation
features.description: Check DAX measures against independent expectations, including SQL calculations over managed Lakehouse or Warehouse sources.

features.title: Verified Report deployment
features.description: Deploy the same authored Report to different destinations, resolving and verifying its intended model and workspace binding.

features.title: Central Fabric Catalogue
features.description: Query installed definitions, signatures, metadata, dependencies and operational state in one Fabric Warehouse.

features.title: Unified Health
features.description: See current, stale, pending, failed or inconsistent work across the registered managed estate.

features.title: Logging and statistics
features.description: Inspect workflow history, Load counts, timings, row changes and recorded outcomes.

features.title: Fault-tolerant execution
features.description: Retain completed effects, record failures and blocked work, and optionally continue independent Load branches.

features.title: Selective execution
features.description: Select installed Load work by whole-name regex, deliberately add ancestors/descendants and preview the selection.

features.title: Controlled concurrency
features.description: Cap one invocation or tune per-resource limits while scheduling independent work in dependency order.

features.title: One command
features.description: weaver catalogue-dashboard deploys the semantic model and Report beside the catalogue, and brings them up to date on the next run.

features.title: Live over Direct Lake
features.description: The dashboard reads the catalogue over Direct Lake, so its pages reflect the latest recorded results. Import mode reads more than ten catalogues.

features.title: Free to tweak
features.description: It is an ordinary Power BI Report. Tweak it to fit your needs, or throw it away and build your own over the catalogue.

features.title: One project, multiple environments
features.description: Keep source files and logical identities while workspace configuration selects physical item and model destinations.

features.title: Incremental Build
features.description: Reconcile changed source-data definitions and affected selected descendants, retaining certified unchanged source work.

features.title: Build previews
features.description: Inspect selected actions, physical targets and destructive effects through a read-only Build plan.

features.title: Controlled deployment bundles
features.description: Review and hand off frozen, destination-specific installation plans without replanning during Install.

features.title: Cross-engine publication and readiness
features.description: Order supported OneLake publication and SQL endpoint-readiness barriers before dependent cross-engine consumers.

features.title: Protect important data
features.description: Keep irreplaceable sources outside managed targets and use Build replacement guards for protected owned objects.

features.title: Run several steps from a notebook
features.description: In Python, `with weaver.workflow():` runs Build, Load, Test and Health on one Session under one workflow ID, in a Fabric notebook or on a desktop.

features.title: Rerun only what is behind
features.description: Load and Test with --stale run only the objects that failed, are pending or are behind their upstream, so recovery repeats as little work as possible.

features.title: Query an item without changing state
features.description: weaver execute runs a T-SQL, Spark SQL, Python or DAX query against one Lakehouse, Warehouse or semantic model and returns the result. It records nothing in the catalogue.

features.title: Several teams on one Dashboard
features.description: One Dashboard can read several teams' catalogues, show which workspaces supply which, and narrow every page by workspace, item and object in the Filters pane.

features.title: Static pages for sharing
features.description: Export every page as static HTML, from the CLI or a notebook, so results can be shared and opened without a running Fabric capacity.

features.title: Work across teams' catalogues
features.description: Give Health, Load or Test several teams' catalogues. Weaver joins them through the shortcuts between workspaces, so a failure is traced across teams and a load runs as one graph.

features.title: Teams that read one another's data
features.description: Workspaces can read one another's data in a loop. Weaver orders the loop, reports it and still traces a failure to every object in it.
